decisions.quote: In this study, we replicated a targeted professional development approach that included a brief one‐on‐one training session and emailed visual performance feedback to increase novice teachers’ use of behavior‐specific praise, an evidence‐based classroom management skill. Dependent variables collected through direct observation included teachers’ behavior‐specific praise along with average student engagement and disruptions.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files were checked and are absent for this never-adjudicated work. The supplied primary source (10.1002/pits.22106) is abstract-only and states that the authors replicated a targeted professional development approach (brief one-on-one training plus emailed visual performance feedback) to increase novice teachers' behavior-specific praise in a multiple-baseline single-case design with four elementary teachers. Shipped row 209 (Gage, MacSuga-Gage, & Crews, 2017, 'Increasing Teachers’ Use of Behavior-Specific Praise Using a Multitiered System for Professional Development', 10.1177/1098300717693568, verified in Crossref metadata) shares two authors (Nicholas A. Gage and Ashley S. MacSuga-Gage) and the behavior-specific praise intervention topic. However, because the abstract supplies no citation, author names, year, title, or reference list for the replicated study, primary evidence does not settle the exact bibliographic identity of the target study or whether it is shipped row 209 versus another prior targeted PD study.
